articles.title: Americas First: Trump and Latin America
articles.summary: While Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s recent travels to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru faced criticism regarding legal overreach and geopolitical tension, the article argues that the United States must prioritize deep economic and security partnerships in Latin America to counter China’s growing influence.
articles.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s most recent expedition to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru — his fifth trip crisscrossing the region as secretary — drew familiar criticism. Washington has made the Western Hemisphere a centerpiece of U.S. foreign policy, raising questions over legal overreach, anti-China arm-twisting, and the revival of backyard geopolitics.

Some of those concerns about tactics have merit. But Rubio is right to prioritize this neighborhood.

At its heart, foreign policy should keep Americans safe, prosperous and free. No other region touches American lives so directly and at such scale. For decades, Washington “rediscovered” Latin America only when migration surged, drugs spilled north, or a rival power moved in. That entire approach is gets it backwards.

Start with prosperity. In 2024, U.S. trade in goods and services with Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean reached $2.32 trillion — nearly one-third of all U.S. trade. That is more than U.S. trade with the European Union and United Kingdom combined. Much of this commerce moves directly by truck, rail and pipeline across a continent we share.

The region also shapes U.S. security, first, through pressure on U.S. borders. U.S. authorities recorded about 2.2 million southwest-border encounters in fiscal 2024. A year later, the number had fallen to roughly 444,000. Despite the swing, both figures make the point: what happens in Latin America does not stay there. Not to mention, more than one half of all immigrants living in the United States were born in Latin America, compared with only about 27 percent in Asia .

The drug trade follows the same map. Mexico’s Sinaloa and Jalisco New Generation cartels are the principal suppliers of fentanyl and other illicit drugs entering the U.S. Of the cocaine samples seized in the U.S. and analyzed by the DEA in 2024 , 84 percent traced back to Colombian coca. Yes, it is worth debating the effectiveness — and legality — of U.S. boat strikes on suspected drug trafficking vessels. But that debate should not obscure the larger truth: These networks cannot be broken without coordination across the Americas.

Energy tells the opposite story: Geography creates strategic advantage. Pipelines and power lines already stitch the continent together. Canada sent the United States about 4.1 million barrels of crude oil a day in 2024, and the U.S. sent Mexico a record 6.4 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day. North American energy integration cushions global shocks. The reason Americans have felt the financial pain of the Iran war much less than other countries is that only about 2 percent of U.S. petroleum consumption depends on crude moving through Hormuz, nearly 90 percent of which flows to Asia instead.

Critical minerals could become the modern version of that energy advantage. Under the mountains and deserts of the Americas lie major deposits of lithium, copper, nickel, graphite, niobium, and rare earths. Yet China still dominates mining and the chokepoint that matters most: processing. The International Energy Agency says China is the leading refiner for 19 of 20 key strategic minerals . The U.S. has the opportunity to link mines to refineries to factories across the hemisphere — and loosen Beijing’s grip on the industries of the future.

Beijing understands the stakes and actively influences the region. China is already the largest goods-trading partner of Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Peru and most other countries in the region. Chinese companies have helped build 37 ports . Those ports move containers today. In a military crisis, some could provide eyes, ears and logistical footholds for Beijing .

So Washington is right to pay attention, but it should do so with some humility and consistency. Latin American countries do not want orders to choose between Washington and Beijing. China buys their copper, soybeans, lithium, and shrimp. It finances roads, ports and infrastructure that Americans too often declined to build. It is worth listening to our neighbors when they express wariness over instruments of U.S. realpolitik .

The answer is not another Monroe Doctrine where Washington seeks to dominate the hemisphere. It is to compete, be the better partner, invest more, trade more. It is to help build ports, power grids, and mineral-processing plants — and, unlike the Chinese, respect local workers and the environment.

It is to share intelligence where interests align and strengthen local security forces — as Rubio wisely did on this trip — rather than threatening to fight criminal gangs ourselves. Treat sovereign governments as partners, not squares on a geopolitical chessboard.

America should not seek to control its hemisphere, but it can no longer afford to neglect it.

Anja Manuel is executive director of Aspen Strategy Group and Aspen Security Forum. She is a former diplomat, author and advisor on foreign policy.

articles.title: Carney says he’s prepared for ‘extreme tail risk’ of US invading Canada
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a new interview that he had geared up for an “extreme tail risk” of the U.S. invading his country, comments arriving in the wake of recent trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa. The Canadian leader, in a New York Times interview published Wednesday, was asked about President Trump’s…
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a new interview that he had geared up for an “extreme tail risk” of the U.S. invading his country, comments arriving in the wake of recent trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa.

The Canadian leader, in a New York Times interview published Wednesday , was asked about President Trump’s push to acquire the U.S.’s northern neighbor. In response, Carney implied that he’d looked into the chance of military action led by the U.S. in depth, but he did not give specifics, according to the outlet.

“I think you have a responsibility in these roles to look at extreme tail risk. That’s just risk management. That’s not a base case,” Carney told the Times, adding that “it would be irresponsible not to” be prepared.

Tensions between Washington and Ottawa intensified in recent months after trade negotiations between the two countries fell apart. Trump launched a tariff war in response, with the U.S. and Canada slapping tariffs on each other’s goods.

Trump has also repeatedly pushed to acquire the U.S.’s northern neighbor, which Canada has rebuffed.

Earlier this month , Carney said his country had overrelied on “easy” economic links with the U.S.

“The past 40 years has been a period of deeper economic integration with the United States. Truth is, it was easy business, but it meant we relied too much on one economic partner. It’s clear that time is over,” Carney said in a video posted to YouTube at the time.

“This is why our plan, since I came into office, has been development and diversification, not denial, waiting to go back to some good old days, and not continued dependence,” he added.

articles.title: Ms Rachel defends her activism by pointing to Mister Rogers' political legacy on children's TV
articles.summary: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel cited Fred Rogers' civil rights pool scene and nuclear arms race episodes to defend her own political activism.
articles.body: Children's YouTube personality Ms. Rachel hit back at critics of her political activism during an interview Tuesday, pointing to Mister Rogers, who she said was very political. Ms. Rachel, whose full name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, spoke to Kareem Rahma, host of "SubwayTakes," and broke down her hottest takes. "Mr. Rogers was political," she said. Mister Rogers, whose full name was Fred Rogers, is known for "Mister Rogers' Neighborhood," a children's program that ran from 1968-2001. MS RACHEL CLAIMS CELEBRITIES SILENT ON GAZA WOULD ‘PROBABLY’ SPEAK IF CHILDREN ‘WERE WHITE’ Ms. Rachel pointed to an example in the children's show in which Rogers invited Officer Clemmons, a Black character, to cool off in a small wading pool during the civil rights movement. The episode aired in 1969, at a time when some public pools still prohibited Black swimmers. Rahma called the episode "revolutionary." YOUTUBE STAR MS RACHEL DECLARES 'I AM POLITICAL' IN NEW MISSION TO SHUT DOWN ICE FACILITY "I've read that some people saw it and in their family it wasn't okay to share a pool, and they were like, 'Oh Mr. Rogers is doing it. It's okay for our family now.' And so it did make a difference and actually people sometimes say to me or you know, in the media, they'll be like, ‘Ms. Rachel should be like Mister Rogers and not be political.' And actually he was political so much on the show. I think maybe they didn't watch it or maybe weren't paying attention because he did so many things," Ms. Rachel said. Ms. Rachel also pointed to a series of episodes from 1983, telling Rahma that Rogers was against the nuclear arms race. "He was against the nuclear arms race, and he had in his neighborhood make-believe he had King Friday building bombs because he thought the other neighborhood Southwood was building bombs, so he wanted to have 100 million and one bomb parts for his bombs and in the show. And then he was like, 'Now we don't have money for the music program because you spent it all on bombs. Queen Sarah, the wife, was like, ‘Why did you spend the tax money on bombs? We should have spent it on these other awesome things,’" Ms. Rachel said. She noted that Mister Rogers also testified before the Senate in support of funding for public broadcasting. "Nixon wanted to cut $10 million from the PBS budget and he testified in front of the Senate and he just shared from his heart how much care goes into his show and how he helps children manage, and feelings are manageable and mentionable, and it was huge and the very like-grrrrrr Senate guy was like, ‘You got your $20 million.’ And it was so touching. It's like the coolest video," Ms. Rachel said. She added, "And so he went to Senate and was like, 'No, government, don't cut funding to PBS.' Like, how political is that?" MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH Author and psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Fred Rogers addressed serious social issues. His 1969 pool scene with Officer Clemmons was a powerful statement about racial equality. But there’s a difference between quietly modeling human dignity and turning your enormous platform with children and parents into a vehicle for your positions on today's political controversies." Alpert continued, "Rogers didn't need to tell his audience, 'Here is the correct political position.' He showed a Black neighbor that he was welcome in his pool. The lesson was contained in the act itself. Ms. Rachel is far more explicit about telling the public what she believes about Gaza, immigration and other politically charged issues. I think invoking Mister Rogers gives her a convenient defense: If Mister Rogers was political, then criticism of her activism can be dismissed as hypocrisy. But that's a false equivalence. You can admire what Rogers did in 1969 without concluding that every children's entertainer therefore has a mandate to become a political activist." YOUTUBE STAR MS RACHEL GIVES FUNDS TO DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED ROSIE O’DONNELL RANTS THAT TRUMP-ERA ICE FACILITIES ARE CONCENTRATION CAMPS WHERE INMATES ARE RAPED Alpert said Rogers was "influential precisely because he didn't beat people over the head with his politics." "He trusted the audience to understand the lesson. The pool scene didn't come with a lecture or a list of political demands. He showed people how to behave," Alpert said of Mister Rogers. Fred Rogers Productions did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Ms. Rachel's other takes included one about children in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. "No child should be in immigration detention center ever," she said. "I've talked with some children, and the harm is so obvious." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "And we don't want to be people who abuse children. It's the medical neglect is abuse. So, they're actually abusing children. And some pediatricians I've talked to have even said torture. Some autistic children in there, like keeping the lights on 24 hours, just that they've been unable to go to the bathroom, to poop for nine days. And as parents, it's like, that's so wrong. Like you can't, and there was a girl they neglected that she had this respiratory stuff, and when they took her to the ICU, she had COVID, RSV. Her oxygen was like 52. So the medical neglect is abuse in there," Ms. Rachel said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP ICE did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

articles.title: Xi comes bearing gifts: 2 giant pandas and 100,000 student visas
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping announced at the White House on Thursday he was gifting the U.S. with two giant pandas and invitations for 100,000 U.S. students to study in China. “The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and the Americans,” Xi said, speaking alongside President Trump and other officials from…
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping announced at the White House on Thursday he was gifting the U.S. with two giant pandas and invitations for 100,000 U.S. students to study in China.

“The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and the Americans,” Xi said, speaking alongside President Trump and other officials from the U.S. and China.

“Here, I have a piece of good news. In a few days, two pandas — Ping Ping and Fuchuan — will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people,” the Chinese leader added.

The Atlanta venue has not had pandas among its animals since 2024, when a previous deal with Beijing expired. The panda diplomacy program originally began in 1957 and has been extended periodically to allow the bears to remain in the U.S., according to Congress .

A spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry shared pictures of Ping Ping and Fuchuan on social media.

Xi also announced Thursday that 100,000 young American students would be invited to study in China over the next five years.

“Achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand-in-hand,” he said in a nod to Trump’s campaign slogan “Make America Great Again.”

He added separately, “The hope of China-U.S. relationship lies in our people, and its future lies with the young.”

The gifts come as Xi and Trump undertake the second day of the Chinese leaders’ elaborate state visit to Washington.

In a rare move, the president and first lady Melania Trump greeted Xi and his wife Madame Peng Liyuan on the tarmac of Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening and hosted him for an arrival ceremony on the South Lawn and a military review in the Rose Garden.

The Trump’s will also host Xi and Peng, along with the Chinese delegation, for a three-course state dinner at the White House on Thursday evening.

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes to be transferred to a halfway house
articles.summary: Holmes, 42, was sentenced to more than 11 years in prison for defrauding investors of millions of dollars through Theranos, the failed blood-testing company that she founded.
articles.body: Elizabeth Holmes, who was convicted of fraud for siphoning hundreds of millions of dollars from several high-profile investors, is scheduled to be transferred from a low-security federal prison to a halfway house next year, according to one of her victims. Holmes, 42, defrauded investors of millions through Theranos, the failed blood-testing company that she founded. She was sentenced in 2022 to 11 years and three months in prison. She and her business partner Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani were ordered to pay 12 victims a total of $452 million in restitution. Holmes has been serving that sentence at a low-security prison in Bryan, Texas. The halfway house will provide her greater freedom. Alan Eisenman, one of her victims, said she is to be transferred to the Austin Transitional Center, a halfway house in Del Valle, an unincorporated community that borders Austin, Texas. The Department of Justice is required by law to notify victims of crime of case developments through letters and emails. Scott Taylor, a spokesperson for the Bureau of Prisons, said he could not provide details of Holmes’ confinement, including release plans. Taylor cited safety, security and a Bureau of Prisons policy that says such information can’t be released until after an individual arrives at their designated institution. Eisenman, an early Theranos investor who testified at Holmes’ trial, said he received a message from the Justice Department’s victim notification system Wednesday saying the halfway house transfer would occur in August 2027. Eisenman, a retired financial planner from Texas, invested about $1.2 million with his family in the failed blood-testing company beginning in 2006. He was the smallest investor among a list of high-profile, well-monied investors who included Australian media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Eisenman was unhappy to hear of the planned transfer. “Seems like a gift,” he told NBC News. Holmes owes Eisenman and his wife, Sherrie, almost $150,000 out of a total of $452 million in restitution for all victims of her crimes, according to a court document. So far, he has “not received a penny” from Holmes, he told NBC News. “She was a liar back in 2006,” Eisenman said, “and she’s a liar today.” Eisenman said he hoped Holmes would remain in prison through her scheduled release date of Feb. 22, 2030, after some reductions in the sentence. In March, a judge cut Holmes’ sentence from 135 months to 123 months. According to a court document, the judge agreed with Holmes that she did not personally cause “substantial financial hardship” to her victims. The government had tried to prevent a reduction of her prison time, arguing that Holmes has not accepted responsibility for her crimes, paid minimal restitution and “has the opportunity to reoffend,” according to a court filing. The government told the court that Holmes has continued to tell national media she intends to resume a career in healthcare technology after her release and has been advising her romantic partner on fundraising for his startup, a company that has similarities to Theranos, the court document states. Eisenman added that he’s against Holmes receiving any form of presidential clemency. She filed for a commutation of her sentence last year. It remains pending. Holmes’ attorney during her trial did not respond to a phone message from NBC News requesting comment. ABC News first reported her pending release to the halfway house. The news comes as a documentary about her is about to be released. The documentary by comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim is based on Fielder living with her and her partner for several days before she entered prison in 2023. It recently made its debut at the Telluride Film Festival and is scheduled for full release next month. Eisenman said he also watched the latest trailer for the documentary, “You Can See Everything,” and plans to see it upon its release next month. His concern, he added, is whether it will portray Holmes as a sympathetic figure. “She’s obviously manipulative,” Eisenman said. “If people don’t see that, then they’re blind. She’s the most conniving person I’ve ever met.”
